candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care: participate in quality-improvement and professional-practice activities, evaluate care against standards, and promote accountability and safe care systems.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — nursing peer review and professional practice evaluation
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate nursing peer review from performance appraisal, informal peer feedback, and credentialing by recognizing its systematic assessment of peer nursing practice against professional standards.

options.A: It is the manager's annual employment-performance appraisal focused on attendance, goals, compensation, and job performance.
options.B: It is informal coworker feedback that is not intended to assess nursing practice against professional standards.
options.C: It is a systematic assessment by nursing peers of the quality and appropriateness of nursing care against professional standards of practice.
options.D: It is the credentialing process used to verify an applicant's education and license before employment.

candidate.rationale: ANA describes nursing peer review as a process in which practicing registered nurses systematically assess, monitor, and make judgments about the quality of nursing care provided by peers as measured against professional standards of practice. The focus is nursing practice and quality improvement, accountability, learning, and identification of practice patterns needing improvement. Therefore C is correct. A describes employment performance evaluation, B describes informal peer feedback, and D describes credential verification rather than peer review.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nursing peer review is a systematic peer assessment of nursing-care quality and appropriateness against professional standards, distinct from employment performance evaluation, casual feedback, or credentialing.
candidate.source_document_title: Peer Review Tip: Distinguishing the Difference Between Peer Review, Peer Evaluation, and Peer Feedback
